learning_outcomes.text: Possess the capacity to design, develop, implement, manage, and improve products, systems, and processes in various industrial fields, using appropriate analytical, computational, or experimental techniques.
Apply acquired knowledge to identify, formulate, and solve problems in broad contexts, being able to integrate them while working in multidisciplinary teams.
Understand the impact of engineering on the environment, the sustainable development of society, and the importance of working in a professional and responsible environment.
Communicate knowledge and conclusions, both orally and in writing, to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Possess learning skills that allow continuous study throughout life for adequate professional development.
Incorporate ICT and Industrial Engineering technologies and tools into their professional activities.
Organization and planning of projects and human teams. Teamwork and leadership capacity.
Applied knowledge of the fundamentals of fluid-mechanical systems and machines.
Know the technologies related to reciprocating engines. Analyze and design fluid-mechanical components and processes that take place in internal combustion engines.
Analyze and conceptually design thermo-fluid-mechanical components and processes that take place in internal combustion engines.
Know the technologies related to the auxiliary systems of reciprocating engines.
Know the technologies in the field of testing and application of reciprocating engines.
Know the operating cycles of reciprocating internal combustion engines.
Know the requirements and properties of fuels used in engines.

syllabus_topics: Potential and weaknesses of IC reciprocating engines.
Fundamental differences between SI and CI engines.
LUBRICATION AND MECHANICAL LOSSES IN ENGINES
Procedures for measuring mechanical losses in engines.
Effect of different engine aspects on charge renewal.
Characteristic parameters vs. load and speed (Synthesis).
Conventional combustion process in CI engines.
Control of the conventional combustion process in CI engines.
Introduction: Requirements for fresh charge in SI engines.
POLLUTANT EMISSIONS, REDUCTION TECHNIQUES AND REGULATIONS.
Reduction techniques for main pollutant emissions.
Regulations and control of pollutant emissions.
Negative torque zone. Application to industrial vehicles.

assessment_methods.method: Global Ordinary Written Exam (covering all topics)
Global Extraordinary Written Exam (resit, covering all topics)

assessment_rules: To pass the course, a minimum grade of 5 out of 10 is required via either the progressive evaluation system or a global exam. The progressive system consists of three written exams: Topics 1-5 (16.7% problems, 16.7% theory), Topics 6-9 (33.3% theory), and Topics 10-13 (33.3% theory), requiring a global grade of 5+ and minimum scores in each activity. Alternatively, a single 100% global written exam, also needing 5+ points, is available for ordinary and extraordinary calls. Mandatory laboratory practices must be attended for any evaluation path, and non-attendance prevents passing the course.
